paper.title_en: False Periodicities in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts Caused by Burst Clustering
paper.abstract_en: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients with high brightness temperatures, but their physical origin remains uncertain. The association of FRB 200428 with a Galactic magnetar provides compelling evidence that at least some FRBs originate from magnetar-like systems. Nevertheless, periodic modulation associated with neutron-star rotation has not been robustly detected in extragalactic FRBs. Motivated by the reported 1.7 s periodicity in the active repeater FRB 20201124A, we conduct a systematic search for short-timescale periodicity in four highly active repeating FRB sources. We employ a sliding-window method that analyzes temporally adjacent bursts within restricted time intervals, allowing transient or intermittent periodic signals to be identified. The search yields apparent period candidates with nominal Poisson-calibrated significances comparable to that reported for the 1.7 s signal, although the inferred periods vary substantially among sources and observing windows. We then perform a nonparametric waiting-time randomization test, in which the observed waiting-time distribution is preserved while the temporal ordering is destroyed. The randomized sequences reproduce the main candidate-period structures seen in the data, demonstrating that these apparent periodicities can arise from the non-Poissonian waiting-time statistics rather than from a coherent periodic process. Rotation-modulated epidemic-type aftershock sequence simulations provide a complementary parametric illustration of the same effect. We therefore find no robust evidence for a short intrinsic periodicity in these data, and the reported 1.7 s signal is not uniquely distinguished from clustering-induced candidates. Robust periodicity searches must evaluate significance against null models that account for the observed waiting-time statistics and the full search procedure.
